_about: Seconds per character for each Olivia variant - the first row of the mode's timing table, which every later timing rule derives from (PHASE_PLAN.md section 3.2, step 2 criterion 2.6). Measured by Hamlet's own Olivia demodulator on the mode author's clean fixtures (work instruction 361 task 5, decision N), and read at startup through OliviaData.Timing.
confirm: done: work instruction 361 task 5 measured it; TheOliviaDemodulatorTests.TheTimingTableIsMeasuredByTheDemodulator holds each row within 2% of the demodulator's own figure
written_by: work instruction 358 task 5, measured by work instruction 361 task 5
method: Each clean fixture is read by OliviaDemodulator with the variant and center its RSID burst announced. Seconds per character is the time from the first decoded block's start to the last decoded block's start, over the characters the blocks before the last one carried: the slope, so the idle padding of a short final block is not charged to every character. The 8/250 row is measured on olivia-8-250-cq-rsid.wav; olivia-8-250-qso-norsid.wav is the blind search's and is reported, not used.
cap_method: PSK31's own rules, counted in characters and then charged at the variant's rate (PHASE_PLAN.md section 3.2, step 4 criterion 4.4, work instruction 365 decision AV). PSK31 seconds per character is Psk31Modulator.SecondsFor over the four framed macros of decision AR - CQ, Answer, Report and Confirm for KC3QIS and W1AW - less each one's idle and reference symbol (32 + 16 + 1 bits at 31.25 baud), over their 219 characters: 0.246941 s. The macro count is floor(30 s / that) = 121, the typed-line count floor(60 s / that) = 242, and the patience count ceiling(7.84 s / that) = 32, where 7.84 s is Psk31Macros.AnswerSeconds(W1AW, KC3QIS), R18's stated PSK31 equivalent of one slot and the only patience the tree states. A variant's cap and patience are these counts times its seconds per character, so 8/250 gets 82.60 s for a macro, 165.19 s for a typed line and 21.85 s of patience, and no rule here is ever a figure in seconds. OperatorSend.LongestUnslottedSeconds, 30 s, is unmoved and still bounds every PSK31 send. The framed Report is 96 characters, 66.03 s at 8/250, and fits. Measured and written by work instruction 365 task 4; the counts are the arbiter's by decision AV and overrulable.
retire_about: The retire window of step 3 criterion 3.4 (work instruction 364 decision AJ): an Olivia channel is retired once this many of its variant's seconds per character have passed since the end of its last accepted block, so the window scales with the variant (PHASE_PLAN.md section 3.2) and is never a figure in seconds. Decision AJ set 24 and said to raise it to the smallest whole number that retires nothing mid-transmission on any shipped fixture. Unit364Trace measured the longest the listener goes without learning of a new accepted block while its station is still sending: 8.14 s on every clean file (12, 16 and 20 characters at 8/250, 16/500 and 32/1000) and 28.24 s = 55.2 characters of 16/500 on olivia-16-500-qso-snr-16db.wav, whose reader shows 9 blocks of 77. So 56: windows 38.23 s, 28.67 s and 22.94 s. The arbiter's number, raised by the arbiter's own rule; overrulable.

estimated_before.method: From assets/fixtures/olivia/manifest.json alone: each fixture's seconds, less 2.32 s where rsid is true, divided by the number of characters in its text, each newline counted as one; for 8/250 the straight line through both 8/250 fixtures (0.683 s per character plus 0.72 s fixed). Work instruction 358 task 5.
estimated_before.why_it_overstated: A fixture's length includes whatever the transmitter sends before the first character and after the last - preamble, tail and the padding that completes the final block - so a length divided by a character count overstates the per-character time, and a short text overstates it most.
